title: Replace lore init's yes/no agent-bridge questions with one multi-select
description:
Direct user instruction, relayed via opum-agent: replace the interactive wizard's sequential yes/no questions for Claude/Codex/Hermes agent bridges with a single multi-select TUI listing all supported instruction files, matching Backlog.md's src/cli.ts (~line 1044) pattern -- @clack/prompts multiselect, one labelled option per instruction file, required: false, explicit clack.isCancel() handling.

Scope: replaces exactly the three confirm() calls at src/commands/init.ts:892/901/904 (Claude, Codex, Hermes bridge questions) with one multiselect prompt. Does NOT touch the git-init question, tracker question, migrate-or-pin question, jira config, docs-site scaffold question, or Obsidian question -- those stay as their existing confirm()/choose() prompts. Does NOT add new harness targets (no gemini/copilot) -- opum-agent was explicit this is a prompt-shape change, not a capability expansion; a larger option set is a separate decision. Does NOT change lore init --codex, which stays as public product surface for external Codex CLI users. Does NOT change skill_source=plugin semantics -- the multi-select chooses which instruction FILES to write, not whether a per-repo skill is generated.

Coordinated with quest-cli directly (per opum-agent's instruction to agree the shape between the two repos rather than implement independently) before starting: library (@clack/prompts), message wording ('Select instruction files to write (space toggles, enter accepts)'), required:false/empty-selection-legal semantics, and explicit cancel handling are AGREED IDENTICAL between lore-cli and quest-cli. lore's option set has a third entry (Hermes/.hermes.md) that quest's doesn't -- confirmed as a real, expected scope difference (which instruction files each CLI knows how to write), not a divergence to resolve.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The three sequential confirm() questions for Claude/Codex/Hermes bridges are replaced by one @clack/prompts multiselect offering exactly the available bridges (gated by the existing detectAgentAvailability() check, same as today)
An empty selection is legal (required: false) and proceeds with no bridge set up, matching todays behavior when every question is declined
Ctrl+C/cancel during the multiselect is handled via clack.isCancel() and exits cleanly with no partial workspace state, not a stack trace
The non-interactive/flag path (--agents/--codex/--hermes, --yes) is unchanged -- the multiselect replaces only the interactive prompt
Wording and empty/cancel semantics match quest-cli's implementation of the same prompt, confirmed by direct coordination, not assumed
Existing wizard tests covering the three yes/no questions are updated to exercise the multiselect instead, and lore check + full test suite pass

implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED (2026-09-09). All six ACs met with evidence:
1. Three confirm() calls replaced by one @clack/prompts multiselect (src/commands/init.ts), gated on detectAgentAvailability() same as before.
2. Empty selection legal (required: false), confirmed by unit test 'declining both in one screen configures neither'.
3. Cancellation via clack.isCancel() maps to the SAME interrupted() usage error used for readline EOF -- one consistent contract, not a special case.
4. Non-interactive/flag path untouched -- verified by grep, no changes to the parsed.agents/codex/hermes flag-driven branches.
5. Wording/semantics match quest-cli's QCLI-255 by direct coordination throughout implementation, including a real per-CLI difference (lore's 3rd Hermes option) and per-CLI default-preselection reasoning (both land on 'pre-check what a bare Enter would have picked before' via different but compatible histories).
6. test/init.test.ts and test/cli.test.ts updated (obsolete LCLI-442 sequential-default tests replaced with multiselect-shaped equivalents); full suite 2889 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, lint clean, typecheck clean, lore check 77 files/0 errors.

BEYOND UNIT TESTS: the real architectural risk here -- @clack/prompts' raw-mode terminal UI sharing stdin with the existing readline-based confirm/choose/ask questions -- cannot be exercised by bun test (no real TTY in that environment). Verified directly in a real tmux PTY: multiselect renders correctly (checkboxes, labels), space-toggle works, Enter confirms and correctly hands control back to a freshly re-opened readline interface for the subsequent docs-site/obsidian questions (no hang, no garbled I/O, no double-input), and the final file writes on disk exactly matched the toggled selection (CLAUDE.md + .hermes.md written, AGENTS.md correctly absent after toggling Codex off). Two full end-to-end runs, one hitting an expected downstream validation failure (Quest not initialized) to confirm 'no partial write survives a refusal' still holds with the new prompt in the mix, one completing successfully.

REVISED DEFAULT (2026-09-09, review round 2): pre-check-all-available was wrong. opum-agent's critique: the user's original complaint was tools writing instruction files nobody asked for; pre-checking everything means a bare Enter on a machine with all three binaries on PATH reproduces exactly that failure. My earlier LCLI-442 reasoning (no accidental-pair-from-inattention when everything's visible at once) was true but answered a different question than whether the default should write anything at all. The deciding argument: the user's own wording -- 'a list of the supported ones and they can select and install the ones they want' -- describes active selection, not deselection.

Changed default to empty (nothing pre-checked). Also refactored InitPrompter.multiselect to take an explicit defaultSelected param (mirroring confirm's defaultValue) rather than hardcoding the pre-check logic inside createRealPrompter -- makes the decision live in one place (the wizard call site) and lets both the real implementation and every test double follow it consistently.

Re-verified in a real tmux PTY: unchecked-by-default renders correctly, toggling one on and confirming writes only that file, and a true bare-Enter run writes zero bridge files (clack's own summary line renders 'none' for the empty case -- no custom copy needed, free consistency with quest-cli since both use the same library). Coordinated the reversal with quest-cli before landing; opum-agent separately ruled quest-cli's prior QCLI-254 default (pre-check claude) reversed to match, since that ruling's own premise (a confirm needs SOME resolution on bare Enter) no longer held once required:false made 'select nothing' a legitimate multiselect outcome.

Full suite 2889/1/0, lint/typecheck/lore check all clean. Pushed as a second commit on PR #629 (not yet merged, per opum-agent's 'do not cut a release' -- this stacks with quest's fix and a marketplace hook fix).

LESSON RECORDED (opum-agent, 2026-09-09), generalizes past this task: auto-merge is a decision made in the past that executes in the future. Arming it commits to a PR's CURRENT content and hands the timing to CI -- correct when the content is settled, wrong the moment the content becomes live again (e.g. a design discussion reopens what the PR should contain). Rule: disarm auto-merge on a PR under active discussion when the question reopens, not whenever you next remember it's armed -- checkable at the moment the discussion starts, since that's already when you're thinking about the change.

What actually happened here: #629's auto-merge (armed before this session's design-reversal discussion started) landed the wrong 'pre-check everything' default onto dev while the reversal was being worked out, before the fix was pushed. Caught and fixed cleanly (rebase dropped the redundant already-merged commit, PR #630 carries just the fix) -- and it never reached main, which is the fast-forward promotion discipline doing exactly what it exists for: dev is where a mistake is cheap, main is where it isn't. A bad merge to dev is not a shipped defect.

opum-agent is recording this as a candidate rule for the opum-sdlc skill (fleet practice, not a lore-cli-specific fact), targeting it for the next opum-workflow release.

BOUNDARY MADE EXPLICIT (2026-09-09), per opum-agent: the auto-merge lesson above is about content UNDER DISCUSSION, not a case against auto-merge itself. Arming it on PR #631 (a settled, tracker-only note) was correct and deliberate, not an oversight -- auto-merge remains exactly the right mechanism whenever a PR's content isn't going to change out from under it. The failure mode of this lesson collapsing into 'never use auto-merge' would cost a genuinely useful mechanism to fix a narrow problem; the rule is specifically 'disarm it the moment a PR's content reopens for discussion,' not 'don't arm it.'

SEQUENCING LESSON (2026-09-09), from opum-agent, generalizing today's auto-merge finding past auto-merge itself: don't leave a PROMOTION sitting under a decision that could reopen, same reasoning as not leaving a merge armed over a live question. Applied without being told: landed the pending dev->main promotion (PR #632, multiselect work) BEFORE starting OPAG-69's fleet-operating-block edit, specifically so the promotion wouldn't sit exposed while unrelated new work was in flight on the same repo. The rule generalizes: 'don't leave a not-yet-final action committed to executing later while its context might still change' -- applies to auto-merge, to a promotion, and presumably to anything else with a similar past-decision/future-execution shape.
